note: evidence: O = first-party official, R = research paper/preprint, M = media/secondary. weight biases ranking. topical = the feed only publishes Physical AI material, so its items need no anchor term. lang = the language a feed publishes in, when it is not English; its titles and excerpts are quoted as written.

filters.repeat_note: an item already shown within this many days is not picked again; it must cover max_age_days and arxiv.lookback_days, or a post still inside the pool is picked a second time the day it leaves the guard
filters.caps_note: per_source and per_evidence reserve room on the shortlist for other feeds and evidence classes; slots they leave empty are filled afterwards from what they held back, in rank order

press_release.note: an announcement in press-release form (wire copy, 'announces', a ticker) is labelled press_release and ranked this much lower; its evidence class is unchanged. Papers and curated baseline entries are never matched.

highlights.note: the shortlist is the page's highlights: arXiv takes at most this share of --limit (a hard cap, in the fill pass too); 'official' reserves a slot for the best qualifying O item and 'hot' for the best qualifying non-arXiv item marked trending. A reservation passes every other gate; one that nothing can fill stays empty and the run log says so (history quota.unmet).

arxiv.lookback_note: the API dates a paper by its first submission; Monday's announcement carries papers submitted from Thursday 18:00 UTC, so a three-day lookback missed them

feeds_note: Added 2026-10-25 after a read-only check (the feed answers 200 and parses; robots.txt allows the URL for physical-ai-radar). keywords keeps only entries naming one of the feed's terms, before max_entries_per_feed (the taxonomy anchors are too loose for a general source: 'cosmos' let an Azure Cosmos DB post through); max_entries 1 keeps a release feed to its newest release; title_prefix names the project in front of a bare release title; repo ties a release feed to its GitHub star count (heat). Not added: Science Robotics eTOC (robots.txt disallows /action/ for every agent), Physical-Intelligence/openpi releases (none, and no tags; its stars still count in heat), 36Kr and 机器之心 (HTML, no feed), robotstart.info and the Agility blog (404), The Robot Report sub-category feeds (403; the main feed is in use), Boston Dynamics, Meta AI and Anthropic (no feed: page_watch candidates once Firecrawl is back, never a browser), X and Reddit (no automation outside their APIs).

heat.note: pairadar.heat: attention, for ranking only, never evidence. cross = independent sources telling one story (same normalised URL, or for non-papers the same story title); hf = Hugging Face Daily Papers upvotes; hn = Hacker News points (Algolia, recent stories); stars = stars per day gained by a tracked repository (radar/heat-state.json keeps the previous count). Each is capped and log-scaled to 0..1 and averaged with components; the score gains weight x heat. trending marks an item with two or more sources or heat >= trending.

page_watch_settings.note: page_watch is the one exception to the machine-readable-endpoint rule: official sources that publish no feed, read only through a self-hosted Firecrawl on a loopback address. RADAR_FIRECRAWL_URL overrides endpoint, and any host other than 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1 is refused. When Firecrawl does not answer the channel is skipped and recorded under `unavailable` in radar/history.json; the run carries on. mode listing: every first-party link under link_prefix is recorded with the day it was first seen; each run offers the ones still inside filters.max_age_days, max_items_per_source at most, least recently offered first, so an overflow comes on the next run. mode page: a changed page becomes one item pointing at the page, dated the run day. A page that cannot be read (including a 5xx with a Firecrawl error code) is that page failing (`page_failed`), never a source-repair target. A standards_watch entry is watched by naming its id in `standards_watch`; its url and title are read from there, never repeated.
